Prerequisite: A FortiSASE remote user subscription (Standard, Advanced, or Comprehensive, sold by number of users) applied to the instance, as a term-based entitlement or a FortiFlex entitlement (a FortiFlex entitlement can be added only to a FortiCloud account with no existing FortiClient Cloud or FortiSASE entitlements)
What it enables: FortiClient agent-based mode and proxy agentless mode (both require user-based licensing), a subscription seat for each managed endpoint, dedicated public IP addresses per security PoP, the Cloud API CASB and DLP license, and the number of security PoPs that remote users can reach (set by the tier and the user band)
How to put it in place: Buy the subscription (FortiSASE Ordering Guide) or create the entitlement in the FortiFlex portal, and apply it to the instance; GUI: System > License overview
Source: FortiSASE 7.4 Administration Guide, "FortiClient agent-based mode using FortiClient", "Proxy agentless mode", "FortiFlex licensing", "Dedicated public IP addresses" (Prerequisites), "Subscription overview", "API-based CASB" (Prerequisites), "Endpoints", and Appendix A, "Number of security data centers accessible per subscription"

Prerequisite: The Advanced or Comprehensive remote users subscription tier
What it enables: Agentless ZTNA, regional compliance rules in geofencing, and log forwarding to SOCaaS (also RBI, the Secure Browser, and the embedded onboarding guide, which are "No direct requirement" rows or no row)
How to put it in place: Buy the Advanced or Comprehensive tier, or upgrade the Standard subscription through Fortinet Customer Service (after an upgrade, request the dedicated public IP addresses through FortiCare Support); GUI: System > License overview
Source: FortiSASE 7.4 Administration Guide, "Agentless ZTNA" (Prerequisites), "Geofencing" (Prerequisites), "Forwarding logs to SOCaaS", "RBI" (Licensing), "Secure Browser", "Embedded onboarding guide" (Prerequisites), and FAQs, "Subscriptions"

Prerequisite: Security PoP add-on subscriptions for more security data centers than the tier and user band include: the Fortinet Security PoP Add-on (1 to 16 locations), and with Comprehensive also the Public Cloud Location Add-on and the Global Region Add-on (up to 20 security data centers in all, except with the Global Region Add-on)
What it enables: Selecting, adding, and changing security PoP locations beyond the number the subscription includes
How to put it in place: Buy the add-on (FortiSASE Ordering Guide); where the instance does not support dynamic infrastructure changes, ask FortiCare Support to add or remove the sites; GUI: Operations > Infrastructure
Source: FortiSASE 7.4 Administration Guide, Appendix A, "Number of security data centers accessible per subscription", and "Infrastructure" (Prerequisites, Instances not supporting dynamic infrastructure changes)

Prerequisite: A FortiGate SPA hub for each service connection: a FortiGate SD-WAN hub built to Fortinet's SD-WAN best practices, or a FortiGate NGFW converted to a standalone IPsec hub (with Fabric Overlay Orchestrator on FortiOS 7.2.4 or later), each with an SPA Service Connection subscription and registered in the same FortiCloud account as FortiSASE, with its IPsec and BGP side configured and its policies allowing the security PoPs
What it enables: Secure private access service connections (up to 12 hubs), and what is reached through them: agentless ZTNA applications, endpoint-to-endpoint traffic through a hub, PKI-authenticated service connections, and LDAP, RADIUS, FSSO, and log servers with the Private access type
How to put it in place: Buy the SPA Service Connection subscription for each FortiGate, register the FortiGate in the FortiSASE FortiCloud account, and configure the hub (FortiOS settings, to the FortiGate STIG); GUI: Operations > Connectivity > Secure private access
Source: FortiSASE 7.4 Administration Guide, "SPA" (Prerequisites, SPA subscription and account prerequisites, Restricting access using a FortiGate SPA hub/spoke policy) and "Agentless ZTNA" (Prerequisites)

Prerequisite: A FortiSASE On-Ramp Location subscription on a Standard, Advanced, or Comprehensive subscription, a FortiSASE subscription for each certified IPsec branch device, and the branch FortiGate (iBGP, BGP per overlay) or third-party IPsec device (static routes) on a supported model and firmware, configured with the matching IPsec settings; the BGP network configuration is set first, and dedicated public IP addresses must be enabled after an upgrade from Standard
What it enables: Branch On-ramp IPsec connections from branch FortiGate and third-party devices
How to put it in place: Buy the subscriptions, register the devices, and configure the IPsec side of each branch device; GUI: Operations > Connectivity > On-ramp tunnel
Source: FortiSASE 7.4 Administration Guide, "On-ramp tunnel" (Prerequisites and considerations: Supported models and firmware, FortiCloud account prerequisites, Network topology)

Prerequisite: Edge devices on supported models and firmware, registered to the same FortiCloud account used to log in to FortiSASE, each with its license: a FortiSASE ThinEdge License for each FortiExtender (and FortiBranchSASE), and a FortiSASE subscription for each FortiGate LAN extension and each FortiAP
What it enables: Authorizing and managing FortiExtender, FortiGate, and FortiAP edge devices (an unlicensed FortiAP cannot be authorized), and so the captive portal for their users
How to put it in place: Buy the licenses, register each device and its license in FortiCloud, and connect the device to the internet; GUI: Operations > Connectivity > Edge devices (Authorization)
Source: FortiSASE 7.4 Administration Guide, "Edge devices" (FortiExtender, FortiGate, and FortiAP Prerequisites: Supported models and firmware, FortiCloud account prerequisites) and "FortiAP" (Considerations of authorizing a FortiAP)

Prerequisite: A SAML identity provider (Microsoft Entra ID, AD FS, Okta, or FortiAuthenticator), preferably one that enforces CAC, with FortiSASE configured in it as the service provider and a group claim in its assertion; for administrators, external IdP roles in FortiCloud
What it enables: SAML SSO for agent and proxy users, external IdP administrators, SSO before the agentless ZTNA portal, authenticated onboarding, FIDO2 and the FortiClient built-in browser for SAML, SCIM provisioning, IdP metadata import, and ZTNA automatic login with Entra ID
How to put it in place: Create the FortiSASE application in the IdP with the Entity ID and Assertion Consumer Service URL from FortiSASE; GUI: Access & authentication > Authentication Sources > SSO (IdP Entity ID, IdP Certificate)
Source: FortiSASE 7.4 Administration Guide, "Supporting external IdP users", "SSO" (Entra ID, AD FS, Okta, and FortiAuthenticator sections), "Authenticated onboarding", and "SCIM server support"

Prerequisite: An LDAP directory (Active Directory or another LDAP server) reachable from the security PoPs at a public address, or behind an SPA hub (P4) with the Private access type, over LDAPS (port 636 by default) with its CA certificate imported; for IPsec agent tunnels, an instance with FortiClient 7.4 support for EAP for LDAP authentication
What it enables: LDAP authentication of remote users, and LDAP authentication for IPsec agent tunnels
How to put it in place: Allow the security PoPs to reach the directory; GUI: Access & authentication > Authentication Sources > LDAP (Access Type, Secure Connection, Server Identity Check)
Source: FortiSASE 7.4 Administration Guide, "LDAP" and "IPsec remote agent support" (EAP for LDAP authentication)

Prerequisite: A RADIUS server reachable from the security PoPs at a public address (port 1812 open) or behind an SPA hub, with the FortiSASE public IP address as an authorized NAS client and the shared secret, patched to use the message-authenticator attribute (CVE-2024-3596)
What it enables: RADIUS authentication of remote users, and the RADIUS server timeout
How to put it in place: Add FortiSASE as a NAS client on the RADIUS server; GUI: Access & authentication > Authentication Sources > RADIUS (Secret, Test connection)
Source: FortiSASE 7.4 Administration Guide, "RADIUS" (Prerequisites)

Prerequisite: An FSSO collector agent (FortiAuthenticator, or the collector agent on a Windows domain controller) reachable from the security PoPs over the internet or an SPA connection on TCP port 8001, with the shared password and the CA certificate of the agent's SSL certificate
What it enables: Fortinet single sign-on user groups in policies, for domain-joined Windows clients behind edge or Branch On-ramp devices
How to put it in place: Set up the collector agent and allow inbound TCP 8001 to it; GUI: Access & authentication > Authentication Sources > Fortinet Single Sign On (FSSO) (Server, Password, Certificate)
Source: FortiSASE 7.4 Administration Guide, "Fortinet Single Sign On (FSSO)" (Prerequisites, Considerations)

Prerequisite: An Active Directory domain that the FortiSASE Endpoint Management Service can reach: an AD server at a public IP address or FQDN, or an AD connector on a Windows host with access to the AD server and outbound internet access (on an instance supporting FortiClient 7.4); or an Entra ID domain with Windows endpoints running FortiClient 7.2.14 or later joined to it
What it enables: Endpoint profile assignment by AD users and groups, the AD connector for a private AD server, and the AD access that pre-logon tunnels give domain-joined Windows machines
How to put it in place: Create the AD connection account, or install the AD connector and save its connector API key; GUI: Access & authentication > Authentication Sources > Domains (LDAPS connection, Use connector)
Source: FortiSASE 7.4 Administration Guide, "Domains", "Entra ID domains", "Active Directory connector" (Prerequisites), and "Pre-logon tunnel"

Prerequisite: Certificates from the DoD PKI: the CA certificates that FortiSASE must trust (LDAPS, FSSO agent, TLS syslog server, PKI peers), a subordinate CA certificate and key for SSL deep inspection, certificates for the agentless ZTNA custom domain and the SAML service provider, machine certificates for pre-logon tunnels, and your CA certificate for signing the preconfigured FortiClient installer
What it enables: Trusted LDAPS, FSSO, and TLS syslog connections, PKI users, deep inspection with a DoD-issued CA, the agentless ZTNA custom domain, pre-logon tunnels, and a signed FortiClient installer
How to put it in place: Request the certificates from the DoD PKI; GUI: System > Certificates
Source: FortiSASE 7.4 Administration Guide, "Certificates", "LDAP" (Certificate), "Fortinet Single Sign On (FSSO)", "Forwarding logs to an external server" (Secure Connection), "PKI", "Uploading a certificate for deep inspection mode", "Pre-logon tunnel" (Prerequisites), and "Managed endpoint client onboarding" (Considerations)

Prerequisite: The FortiSASE deep inspection CA certificate in the trusted root store of the endpoints of agentless proxy users and site-based edge device users (FortiClient installs it automatically for agent-based users)
What it enables: Deep inspection without certificate errors for proxy and edge device users
How to put it in place: Download the CA certificate and distribute it to the endpoints (for example through Group Policy); GUI: Security > Traffic > Security profiles (CA certificate)
Source: FortiSASE 7.4 Administration Guide, "Installing a certificate for deep inspection mode"

Prerequisite: An external log server: FortiAnalyzer (with the FortiSASE security PoPs authorized), a syslog server that accepts TLS over TCP, or a CEF server, reachable at a public address or behind an SPA hub (a private primary server needs a public secondary server); or a FortiAnalyzer Cloud instance with an access token
What it enables: Log forwarding to one or two self-managed servers, log forwarding to FortiAnalyzer Cloud, and keeping logs beyond the FortiSASE retention period
How to put it in place: Set up the log server and allow FortiSASE to reach it; GUI: Operations > Logs > Settings (Log Forwarding to Self-Managed Service, Remote Server Type, Access type, Secure Connection)
Source: FortiSASE 7.4 Administration Guide, "Forwarding logs to an external server" (including the TLS syslog and on-premise FortiAnalyzer examples) and "Forwarding logs to FortiAnalyzer Cloud"

Prerequisite: Onboarding completed in the SOCaaS portal
What it enables: Log forwarding to FortiGuard SOCaaS and its alert triage
How to put it in place: Click Start Onboarding after enabling the setting and complete onboarding in the SOCaaS portal; GUI: Operations > Logs > Settings (Log Forwarding to SOCaaS 24x7 managed security event monitoring)
Source: FortiSASE 7.4 Administration Guide, "Forwarding logs to SOCaaS"

Prerequisite: FortiClient on each endpoint, installed from the preconfigured installer or registered with the invitation code, at the version a feature needs: FortiClient 7.2 or 7.4 for IPsec remote agents (7.4.8 recommended for new instances, 7.2.14 for instances created before 25.4.c), 7.2.0 or later on Windows for pre-logon tunnels, 7.4.4 or later for recording client tags, and an instance with FortiClient 7.4 support for EAP for LDAP authentication
What it enables: Agent-based mode and its tunnels, endpoint management, and the features that need a minimum FortiClient version
How to put it in place: Deploy FortiClient with the preconfigured installer (or through a UEM platform) and keep it at the recommended version; GUI: Operations > Connectivity > Managed Endpoints (FortiClient Version)
Source: FortiSASE 7.4 Administration Guide, "Managed endpoint client onboarding", "IPsec remote agent support", "Pre-logon tunnel" (Prerequisites), "Endpoint management settings" (Prerequisites), and "Endpoint upgrade"

Prerequisite: A FortiGate ZTNA application gateway configured for the private applications, connected to FortiSASE and authorized there (FortiOS 7.4.2 or later for tags learned directly from FortiClient)
What it enables: Agent-based ZTNA: role-based access with the client certificate and security posture tags, learned tags, UDP forwarding, and access keys for gateways in other FortiCloud accounts
How to put it in place: Configure the ZTNA application gateway on the FortiGate (FortiOS settings, to the FortiGate STIG); GUI: Security > Traffic > ZTNA > Agent-based > Connectors
Source: FortiSASE 7.4 Administration Guide, "Agent-based ZTNA" (Configuration workflow) and "Endpoint management settings" (Prerequisites)

Prerequisite: A FortiCare Support ticket that enables a select availability feature or makes a back-end change
What it enables: The select availability features (central management, FortiClient event logs, authenticated onboarding, SCIM, backup and restore, factory reset on non-NFR instances), dedicated IP and IP anchoring changes, and signing the preconfigured installer with your CA certificate
How to put it in place: Open a FortiCare Support ticket for the feature or change
Source: FortiSASE 7.4 Administration Guide, "Select availability features" (the table and each feature's Prerequisites), "Dedicated public IP addresses", and "Managed endpoint client onboarding" (Considerations)

Prerequisite: A FortiManager registered to the same FortiCloud account as FortiSASE, on FortiManager 7.4.4 or later (7.6.4 or later for policy packages), with FortiSASE added to a FortiGate or Security Fabric ADOM
What it enables: Central management of FortiSASE settings from FortiManager, including MSSP tenants with a FortiManager key
How to put it in place: Register the FortiManager in FortiCloud and add the FortiSASE connector in FortiManager; GUI: System > Central management
Source: FortiSASE 7.4 Administration Guide, "Select availability features" (Central management conditions) and "Central Management" (Prerequisites and considerations)

Prerequisite: IPsec remote agent support on the instance (the default on new instances since 24.4.b.1; SSL instances move to it through SSL to IPsec transition mode)
What it enables: IP anchoring, SCIM (not with hybrid IPsec and SSL), the IPsec pre-shared key setting, and EAP for LDAP authentication
How to put it in place: Complete the migration to IPsec; GUI: Operations > Software audit & version
Source: FortiSASE 7.4 Administration Guide, "IPsec remote agent support", "Dedicated public IP addresses", and "SCIM server support" (Prerequisites)

Prerequisite: A UEM platform (Microsoft Intune, Jamf, or Workspace ONE) with the API credentials FortiSASE uses
What it enables: Provisioning ZTNA certificates to enrolled BYOD devices through the UEM platform
How to put it in place: Create the API credentials on the UEM platform; GUI: System > UEM integration (Vendor, Test Connection)
Source: FortiSASE 7.4 Administration Guide, "UEM integration"

Prerequisite: Customer-managed on-premise IPsec or SSL VPN gateways (FortiGate) configured with the FortiSASE custom tunnel settings, and for IPsec with the same pre-shared key as the FortiSASE Cloud Security tunnel
What it enables: Custom tunnels in endpoint profiles, failover gateways, and on-premise devices in regional compliance rules
How to put it in place: Configure the gateway with the tunnel settings for custom IPsec tunnels (FortiOS settings, to the FortiGate STIG); GUI: Endpoint management > Configuration > Global (Pre-shared key)
Source: FortiSASE 7.4 Administration Guide, "Tunnel settings" (FortiClient), "Global" (Pre-shared key), and "Regional compliance"
